lead.tldr: Erebor's national charter approval signals regulatory shift toward crypto banking legitimacy, reducing compliance friction for institutional capital deployment in digital assets. • Continued fundraising momentum ($258M raised) despite 46% Bitcoin drawdown suggests institutional conviction persists despite near-term volatility and miner distress signals. • Vietnam's proposed 0.1% crypto transfer tax creates regulatory clarity but may redirect trading volume to offshore exchanges, fragmenting Asia-Pacific liquidity. • Hong Kong hedge fund contagion risks remain elevated as Bitcoin weakness persists, warranting portfolio stress testing against further leverage unwinds in regional markets.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Despite market volatility, crypto firms continue raising substantial capital with institutional players like Goldman Sachs and Citi leading investments, while regulatory breakthroughs like Erebor's new US bank charter signal growing acceptance of crypto-native financial infrastructure. As Vietnam implements new transfer taxes and regulatory frameworks tighten globally, the landscape is shifting toward compliance-first innovation and institutional-grade solutions.

top_signals.title: Crypto firms raise $258m despite $2 trillion market drawdown
top_signals.summary: Crypto firms raised $258 million in funding this week, including Tether's $100 million investment in Anchorage Digital, TRM Labs' $70 million Series C round, and Jupiter's $35 million from ParaFi Capital, despite a $2 trillion cryptocurrency market drawdown. The deals emphasized infrastructure, with four in DeFi and three in payments, signaling institutional focus on compliance, custody, and blockchain analytics amid regulatory scrutiny. For institutional investors like Goldman Sachs and Citi, this resilient capital inflow from mature players such as Galaxy Digital highlights long-term confidence in crypto's foundational technologies over short-term volatility. These investments matter as they bolster regulated services essential for broader adoption by asset managers and corporations.

top_signals.title: Erebor Secures First New US Bank Charter of Trump's Second Term
top_signals.summary: Erebor Bank, a crypto-focused startup lender, has secured a national bank charter from US regulators. This marks the first new US bank charter granted since Trump's second term and signals increasing regulatory acceptance of crypto-related financial institutions.

top_signals.title: What caused the massive Bitcoin crash? Clues point to a blow-up at Hong Kong hedge funds
top_signals.summary: The article suggests that a blow-up at Hong Kong hedge funds may have contributed to a significant Bitcoin price crash. The piece analyzes potential causes of the market downturn.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin - Is MARA's $87M BTC move more evidence of miner distress?
top_signals.summary: The article discusses whether MARA's $87M BTC move is further evidence of distress among Bitcoin miners. Ongoing miner distress could potentially derail BTC's recovery.

top_signals.title: Vietnam Draft Rules Propose 0.1% Tax on Crypto Transfers
top_signals.summary: Vietnam's draft rules propose a 0.1% tax on crypto transfers, similar to stock trades, while exempting them from VAT. The rules also include strict licensing requirements for crypto exchanges.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, This week has been a pivotal moment for crypto and blockchain innovation. While markets experienced significant volatility, the capital flowing into our ecosystem tells a different story. Crypto firms raised $258 million in funding despite a $2 trillion market drawdown. What's remarkable is where this capital is flowing. Tether's $100 million investment in Anchorage Digital, TRM Labs' $70 million Series C, and Jupiter's $35 million round showcase institutional conviction in infrastructure, DeFi, and payments. These aren't speculative bets. They're strategic commitments to compliance, custody, and blockchain analytics from mature players like Galaxy Digital, Goldman Sachs, and Citi. This is institutional capital voting for the long term. The regulatory landscape is shifting too. Erebor Bank just secured the first new US bank charter of this administration, marking a watershed moment for crypto-focused financial institutions. Regulators are recognizing that blockchain technology and crypto services are essential infrastructure for the digital economy. At Blockwall, we've always believed that downturns separate signal from noise. They reveal which founders are building real solutions and which technologies will power the next generation of the internet. Market volatility doesn't change our thesis: Web3 innovation will reshape how we organize digital value, and the teams building this future deserve capital and support. The resilience we're seeing in funding flows, combined with regulatory progress, suggests we're entering a maturation phase. This is when the real work begins.
